      <title>Premier League: 10 talking points from the weekend’s action</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/oct/26/premier-league-10-talking-points-from-the-weekends-action</link>
      <description><p>Bournemouth’s transfer nous puts United to shame, Araújo is winning admirers at Anfield and Suzuki adapts swiftly at Villa</p><p>The three Bournemouth goalscorers cost a combined £85m, joining from Vasco da Gama, Middlesbrough, and Porto. The Cherries are smart at investing, far more so than Manchester United, who have wasted a lot of money by failing to look outside the box for players like Rayan, Marcus Tavernier and Evanilson. United may not have the wealth they previously showed in the transfer market but Bournemouth are showing what can be done within a budget and, more importantly, will be able to make a profit on signings. United, however, only know losses as everyone’s price tag diminishes the moment they come through the Old Trafford door. Jason Wilcox and others can point to certain factors that are against them but there are quality signings to be made at the right price if you have the ability to find them. <strong>Will Unwin</strong></p><p><em>Match report: <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/oct/25/manchester-united-bournemouth-premier-league-match-report-michael-carrick">Manchester United 0-3 Bournemouth</a></em></p><p><em>Will Unwin: <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/oct/25/manchester-united-michael-carrick-bruno-fernandes-jim-ratcliffe-institutional-failures">Carrick left carrying can for institutional failings</a></em></p><p><em>Match report: <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/oct/24/aston-villa-manchester-city-premier-league-match-report">Aston Villa 2-1 Manchester City</a></em></p><p><em>Match report: <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/oct/25/liverpool-brighton-premier-league-match-report">Liverpool 2-0 Brighton</a></em></p><p><em>Match report: <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/oct/24/chelsea-tottenham-premier-league-match-report">Chelsea 0-2 Tottenham</a></em></p><p><em>Barney Ronay: <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/oct/24/chelsea-tottenham-premier-league-austin-macphee-mike-penders-roberto-de-zerbi">Glitch in Chelsea’s coding costs Alonso while resurgent Spurs are all systems go</a></em></p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/oct/26/premier-league-10-talking-points-from-the-weekends-action">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Fernandes gamble leaves Carrick to carry the can for United’s institutional failures | Will Unwin</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/oct/25/manchester-united-michael-carrick-bruno-fernandes-jim-ratcliffe-institutional-failures</link>
      <description><p>Leaving out his captain was doomed to fail but so are the club under the current leadership and the fans at Old Trafford know that all too well</p><p>Dropping your captain, who has held the team together for most of the past five years, is a bold move from a man whose job is on the line. It was very much a make-or-break decision from Michael Carrick to leave out Bruno Fernandes against Bournemouth. It did not work and Carrick knew the consequences if it failed and will probably pay the price for it, but he should not be alone.</p><p>Carrick said the decision to drop the Portuguese playmaker was purely based on football reasons but criticising his manager after <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/oct/21/como-manchester-united-champions-league-match-report">the desperate defeat to Como</a> cannot have helped. Clearly Carrick disagreed with his captain’s <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/oct/21/michael-carrick-bruno-fernandes-manchester-united-como-champions-league">comments on the lack of pressing</a> in the Champions League fixture. It was somewhat telling that Lisandro Martínez kept his place <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/oct/13/lisandro-martinez-hits-out-at-united-hierarchy-after-defeat-at-atletico-madrid">despite pointing out</a> the director of football, Jason Wilcox, was a hindrance to the club the previous week.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/oct/25/manchester-united-michael-carrick-bruno-fernandes-jim-ratcliffe-institutional-failures">Continue reading...</a></description>
